transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I just can’t keep my mind on one thing anymore. At work, if a saw starts up, or somebody walks past the office, or even if I suddenly think about another job I need to do, I’m off track. Then I lose where I was, and before I know it the whole day’s gotten away from me.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety, like you can't sit still?

Yes, I do. If I’m stuck at the desk doing estimates, or sitting through a long meeting, I get this wound-up feeling inside, like I need to stand up and move around. Even when there’s no reason for it and I know I should just sit there and finish, it’s hard to stay put.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think of myself as doing things without thinking, not in a big way. I might speak too quickly sometimes, but I can’t say that’s a main problem I’ve noticed.
Do you often interrupt others when they're speaking?
I don’t think so, not often. I might jump in now and then if I’m trying to make a point, but I haven’t really noticed interrupting people as a big problem for me.
Do you often have trouble completing tasks or projects?

Yes. Since I’ve been stuck doing more of the shop paperwork, it’s gotten pretty bad. I have bids, schedules, invoices, and the apprentices asking me things, and I can’t seem to sort out what needs to come first. It all piles up on my bench, and then I’m rushing at the last minute and still missing deadlines.
Do you have trouble organizing your time or tasks?

Yes, definitely. I have a hard time figuring out what needs to come first. With all the shop paperwork now—bids, schedules, invoices—and then the apprentices asking me things, it just piles up on my bench. Then I’m rushing around at the last minute and still missing deadlines.
Were you very physically active or restless when you were a child?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember being especially restless as a kid, not in a way that stands out to me. My memory of that is kind of fuzzy.
Did you have trouble paying attention or following instructions when you were in school?

Yes, I did. Even in grade school, before I was 12, teachers would tell my mother I was bright but careless. I’d lose homework, forget what I was supposed to do, or just be staring out the window instead of finishing my work.
Do you often feel the need to be physically active, like running, climbing, or engaging in other intense physical activities, now that you're an adult?

Yeah, I do. Not so much running or climbing or anything like that, but if I have to sit at the desk doing estimates, or sit through a long meeting, I get really wound up inside. I feel like I need to get up and move around, even when I know I’m supposed to just stay put and finish.
Have you experienced these difficulties with attention and restlessness your whole life, or did they start more recently?

It’s gotten to this level more recently. I mean, I had some issues when I was younger, but the really bad trouble has been going on about a year and a month now, since I broke my wrist and got moved into more shop paperwork and supervising instead of doing the hands-on carpentry.
Have these difficulties with attention and restlessness caused problems for you in your relationships or at work?

Yes. At work it’s been a real problem. I’ve made mistakes or gotten behind on things, and it’s cost me commissions. Sometimes jobs have had to be redone because I missed something or didn’t get it handled in time. The crew doesn’t really trust me as much now with scheduling or ordering materials, and that feels awful.

At home, my husband has had to take over the bills and remind me about things, because I keep losing papers or missing what needs to be done. So yes, it’s definitely affecting both.
Have you been feeling overwhelmed, anxious, or depressed lately?

I’m not really sure how to answer that. I mean, I do feel overwhelmed sometimes, but I don’t know if I’d call it anxious or depressed. It’s more like I get frustrated and worn out by trying to keep up.
Did you have any problems with paying attention, following instructions, or being restless when you were a teenager?

Yes, I did. Even before I was a teenager, like in grade school, my teachers would tell my mother I was bright but careless. I’d lose homework, forget what instructions were, or just sit there staring out the window instead of finishing my work. So it wasn’t totally new, no.
Have you ever had difficulty waiting for your turn in lines or when waiting for something?
I don’t really know. I haven’t noticed that as a big problem for me. I might get impatient sometimes like anybody, but I can’t think of it being something that causes trouble.
Do you ever find yourself becoming so focused on a task that you lose track of everything else around you?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I can get into something if I’m working on it, but I don’t know if I’d say I lose track of everything around me. I haven’t really noticed that as a problem.
Did you have any problems with attention or restlessness that you remember being noticed by your parents or teachers before you were 7 years old?

Yes, I think so. I know I’ve said some of this, but even in grade school my teachers would tell my mother I was bright, but careless. I’d lose homework, forget instructions, and instead of finishing my seatwork I’d be staring out the window. I’m not sure about before exactly age 7, but it was definitely early on.
Did your parents ever mention to you that you had trouble sitting still or paying attention when you were very young, like before you started school?

I don’t know about before I started school exactly. What I do remember is that by grade school, definitely before I was 12, teachers were telling my mother I was bright but careless. I’d lose homework, forget instructions, and sit there staring out the window instead of finishing my work.
Do you ever become so focused on something that you ignore everything else around you?
Not really, no. I mean, I can focus if I’m into something, but I don’t think I tune everything out or ignore what’s going on around me. At least not that I’ve noticed.
Did your difficulties with attention and restlessness start when you were a child or did they develop later in life?

They started when I was a child. Like I said, back in grade school, before I was 12, teachers were already telling my mother I was bright but careless. I’d lose homework, forget instructions, and be staring out the window instead of finishing my seatwork.
Have your difficulties with attention and restlessness significantly impacted your ability to function in your daily life or maintain relationships?

Yes, it has. At work, my mistakes and delays have cost me commissions, and sometimes I’ve had to redo parts of jobs because I missed something. The crew doesn’t really want to rely on me for scheduling or ordering materials anymore, because I’ve messed that up enough times.

At home, my husband handles the bills and reminders now. I misplace papers or miss what needs to be done, so he’s had to take that over. It’s caused a lot of stress.
